completed_step: Read-only audit of C35-dimensional route energy features, public energy refresh semantics, route legality and the32 post-depletion assignments.
findings: C contains destination energy, full-frequency current-task CPU energy, source energy, TX energy and signed destination/source margins. The energy features are connected to the actual candidate scorer; no energy-unit mismatch or negative-sign loss was found in the audited scalar path.

Neighbor energy is a causal public payload, refreshed when that node receives a physically attempted link. CPU consumption alone does not refresh it. Actor AoI is available and valid old payloads remain available until refreshed.

Route legality is geometric candidate availability; it does not certify future destination CPU energy or deadline feasibility. The existing C design explicitly preserved A/B legality, so this audit does not identify an implementation deviation in that contract.

All32 assignments were legal argmax choices. Thirty reconstructed published-energy values equal the actual low remaining energy; two overestimate it. Message ages range1-22 slots. Energy equality does not imply all message fields are fresh.

All32 reconstructed full-frequency task-energy margins are negative;31 published energies are even below the quarter-frequency completion-energy lower bound. These are separate tests, because a negative full-frequency margin alone does not prove that a lower frequency is impossible.

The actual extractor preserved low energy and signed negative margins, while cpu_valid and candidate legality remained true as designed. These valid flags describe defined hardware/estimates, not a guarantee of enough energy.
evidence_boundary: Original route logs do not contain full actor input tensors or recurrent hidden states. Energy/time components were deterministically reconstructed from immutable passive records and checked through the production scalar extractor; unrelated inputs were engineering placeholders. No actual actor forward, gradient update, environment replay or alternate policy outcome was generated.
conclusion: Stale information is insufficient as the sole explanation for the32 assignments. The current learned route scorer does not consistently avoid low-energy destinations that remain legal. The audit does not establish that reward must change, that masks should change, or that longer training cannot help.
